quilt-qcells-main/README.md:
# quilt-qcells

CELL-MAPPING implemented as a working modular plugin: **quantum ops as
quilt cells**. Wraps a `micromoth.QuantumCircuit`; as each primitive op
is appended, the corresponding cell row is emitted into an fnv1a-64
hash-chain ledger (genesis prev `0x0000000000000000`). **The ledger is
the circuit** — it replays to a byte-faithful `QuantumCircuit`.

Implements the DESIGN receipt at
`MicroMoth-quilt/docs/CELL-MAPPING.md` (op inventory
`init m x h rx rz cx crx swap`; algebra BIND · LINK · EFFECT · VIEW ·
TICK + adopted FORGET, PROOF). `y`/`z`/`ry`/`t` sugar decomposes at
append time and never enters a ledger.

## Files

- `qcells.py` — the plugin (`CellCircuit` wrapper, `CellLedger`,
  `verify_ledger`, `rebuild_from_rows`, `check_anchor`). Byte-level
  encoding choices the design left open are pinned as canon C1–C6 with
  receipted rationale in the module docstring.
- `conformance.py` — proof harness. `--register` seals claims P1–P4
  (PENDING) + sha256/mtime seals into `registration.json` BEFORE runs;
  runs refuse (fail-closed) on stale seals.
- `registration.json` — the pre-run claim registration (seal discipline).
- `verdict.md` — honest verdict: P1–P4 **PASS**, counts, limits.
- `receipts/` — raw outputs: fnv1a-64 receipt chain, summary with
  per-ledger anchors, 16 raw circuit ledgers.
- `micromoth.py` — vendored byte-identical oracle
  (sha256 `bbd10ac2ffd4dd8b…`, from `SuperInstance/MicroMoth-quilt`
  @ `5eb1619`); pin-checked at every run.

## Run

```bash
python3 conformance.py --register   # once, before the first run
python3 conformance.py              # ALL GREEN or exit 1 (fail-closed)
```

## What it proves / does NOT claim

Proves (P1–P4, all PASS): replay == oracle exactly; chain verifies from
genesis; exhaustive single-byte tamper (4254/4254) localizes to the
exact row; byte-identical determinism across builds and across full
conformance runs.

Does NOT claim: physical erasure (FORGET is receipted tombstone
semantics — the chain is never edited); tail-truncation detection
without the published `(tip, rows)` anchor; exact-amplitude PROOF
witnesses (rounded, digest-pinned); seeded sampling without the global
RNG wrapper; support for ops outside the nine-primitive inventory.
Unseeded counts remain the design's honest hole: they are minted
`EFFECT/UNSEALED` (seed: null) and excluded from every determinism claim.

Python 3 stdlib + `micromoth.py` only. No network calls.

# VERDICT — qcells (task 49-c), CELL-MAPPING implementation

Date: 2026-09-28 (UTC). Lane: 49-c, wave 49, quilt/murmur-protocol.
Repo: `SuperInstance/quilt-qcells`. Oracle: `micromoth.py` `simulate()`
(vendored byte-identical, sha256
`bbd10ac2ffd4dd8bdee86480866107b3c0917ab09286b1d9e2ed144faed482df`,
pin-checked fail-closed at every run).

## Discipline

Claims **P1–P4 were registered in `registration.json` BEFORE the first
conformance run** (status PENDING, sha256 + mtime + size seals over
`qcells.py` / `conformance.py` / `micromoth.py`). Every run re-verifies
the seals and refuses to run (exit 2) if the code moved. The code that
ran is the code that was sealed: `qcells.py` sha256 `fb4f54e7…`,
`conformance.py` sha256 `4643ada3…` — identical at registration and at
the final green run.

## Claim table

| Claim | Statement (abridged) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | Ledger replay reproduces `simulate()` EXACTLY: rebuilt `data` == wrapped `data`; statevector ==; sealed counts == and fold from EFFECT/collapse rows; PROOF + VIEW digests re-derive by replay | **PASS** (16/16 circuits) |
| **P2** | fnv1a-64 chain verifies from genesis `0x0000000000000000` for every ledger; canonical JSON round-trips; only primitive ops in BIND rows (no y/z/ry/t sugar ever enters a ledger) | **PASS** (16/16) |
| **P3** | Single-byte tamper of any ledger row detected fail-closed at exactly the tampered row | **PASS** (4254/4254 localized exact) |
| **P4** | Determinism crown: two independent builds of the same circuit + seed → byte-identical ledgers | **PASS** (15/15 sealed; unsealed honestly excluded) |

## Conformance counts

- Circuits: **16** (Bell, GHZ-3, ry/z+t/y decomposition cases, crx, swap,
  crossed-clbit multi-measure, init flat + init complex, x·x state-return,
  3-layer depth circuit, noise-model case, FORGET case, measure-only edge,
  unsealed honesty case).
- Ledger rows minted: **1418** (BIND gates, LINK boundary, EFFECT
  readout/collapse, VIEW, TICK, PROOF, FORGET — all seven opcodes live).
- Tamper: **4254 cases** (id-flip, kind-flip, prev-flip × every row of
  every ledger; the row-0 prev-flip is the genesis tamper) —
  **4254 localized at exactly the tampered row**, fail-closed.
- Negative controls: **5/5** — forged tail extension (chain passes,
  anchor catches), dropped middle row (fails at the sequence break),
  truncated tail (chain passes, anchor count catches), fully re-forged
  chain with doctored init payload (chain passes, **anchor AND payload
  sha256 pin both fire**), unsealed hole is real (4 unsealed runs disagree).
- Receipt chain: 21 rows, tip `73583aaef12b1d4d`, verified from genesis.
- Byte-identical crown extended: two full conformance runs produced
  **byte-identical `receipts/conformance.jsonl` and `receipts/summary.json`**
  (no wall-clock values enter receipts).

## What this proves (honestly scoped)

- The CELL-MAPPING mapping is implementable as pinned: one
  `QuantumCircuit.data` list IS a cell ledger; the ledger replays to a
  circuit that micromoth's own simulator treats identically.
- The fnv1a-64 chain (genesis prev `0x0000000000000000`, canonical JSON
  encoding — the byte-level encoding was open in the design and is
  pinned with receipted rationale in `qcells.py` C1–C6) is tamper-evident
  with exact row localization.
- Seeded sampling via the global-RNG wrapper (the design's own
  `seeded_counts` mechanism) makes counts replayable byte-exactly;
  unseeded sampling is kept honestly UNSEALED (seed: null) and excluded
  from all determinism claims.

## Honest failures / limits (read before trusting)

- **No failures to hide: all four claims PASS.** The limits below are
  design-honesty choices, not failures.
- FORGET is **tombstone-append, not physical excision** — a strictest-
  honest-reading choice receipted in code: deleting rows from a
  prev-chain breaks every downstream link and destroys the
  tamper-evidence the mapping exists for. Counts are retained; the
  serving surface filters tombstoned collapse records; the FORGET itself
  is a receipted row.
- Hash chains cannot detect tail truncation or well-formed tail
  extension without an out-of-band anchor; `(tip, row_count)` anchors for
  every ledger are published in `receipts/summary.json` and enforced by
  negative controls N1/N3.
- PROOF witnesses pin **rounded** amplitudes (declared precision,
  sha256), not exact amplitudes; exactness lives in the replay-vs-oracle
  equality (P1), not in the digest.
- `initialize()` is refused once any gate exists (it would clear the
  program from under the chain); `measure_all()` and circuit `__add__`
  are deliberately not wrapped.
- micromoth exposes no `__version__`; the simulator pin in every LINK
  boundary cell is the vendored file's sha256 (AUDIT manifest pattern).

## Artifacts

- `receipts/conformance.jsonl` (fnv1a-64 receipt chain, tip
  `73583aaef12b1d4d`), `receipts/summary.json` (claims, totals, anchors),
  `receipts/ledgers/<circuit>.jsonl` (16 raw ledgers).
- Local commit history starts `49-c:`. Remote tip recorded in the wave
  worklog; verification `git ls-remote` == local HEAD is part of the
  publish step.
